ask.where: Only this web app gets it. You can change it later in Settings → Web Apps.
desc.chat: Messages and groups, in a window of its own
store.subtitle: A web app opens in a window of its own, with its icon in the Dock. Each one can have several accounts (profiles), each with its own data.
store.whatHappens: It opens in a window of its own, apart from your browser and from the other web apps. It asks before it uses the camera, the microphone, the screen or your location.
store.untested: Not checked on LordOS yet: some features may not work.
store.installed: {name} is installed. It's in Apps, and you can keep it in the Dock.
store.addHint: LordOS opens the page apart, without any of your data, to read its name and icon. Nothing is installed until you press Install.
store.name: Name
store.badName: Give it a name of up to 64 characters.
store.manifestYes: The site describes itself as a web app.
store.manifestNo: The site doesn't describe itself as a web app: it opens as a page in a window of its own.
store.runtimeTitle: Web apps need the lordos-web package
store.runtimeBody: Web apps run in the LordOS Web Runtime, the lordos-web package, which isn't installed. Install it here; the rest of LordOS works the same without it.
store.address.scheme: Only secure (https) addresses can be added.
store.address.invalid: That doesn't look like a web address.
settings.noRuntime: The lordos-web package isn't installed, so web apps can't open. The Store's Web apps section installs it.
settings.footer: Choose an app to see its profiles, its permissions and how much space it takes.
settings.none: No web apps installed. Get them in the Store.
settings.profilesFooter: Each profile is a separate account, with its own data, cookies and window. The Dock opens the first one; the others are in its right-click menu.
settings.badName: A name of 1 to 64 characters, with no space at either end.
settings.permissionsFooter: Ask: the app asks the first time it needs it, and your answer shows here.
settings.backgroundFooter: Closing the window keeps the app running behind its icon next to the clock, so its notifications still arrive. Quit it from that icon.
settings.wipeOn: Its data goes too: the signed-in session, what the site saved on this computer and its cookies.
settings.wipeOff: Its data stays on this computer: adding it again with the same name brings it back.
